tabs.title: Disclosure and Distance
tabs.description: Analyse how Mara frames silence and personal visibility.

tabs.title: Memory and Attention
tabs.description: Interpret stories collected for the archive.

tabs.title: Invitation without Obligation
tabs.description: Evaluate ethical choices in the letter.

questions.q: Why does Mara reject her usual apology about being busy?
choices: She has already explained her schedule in several messages.
She believes that being busy never affects friendships.
It would conceal the deliberate avoidance behind their superficial contact.
Jules has explicitly forbidden apologies.
questions.explanation: Mara says the apology would falsely make the silence sound accidental.

questions.q: What is implied by Mara's choice to reply to a question about happiness with a sunset photograph?
choices: The appealing image allowed her to avoid a vulnerable answer.
The sunset was intended as a direct statement of unhappiness.
She misunderstood the question as a request for travel photographs.
Her phone prevented her from writing a message.
questions.explanation: Mara calls the photo an easy escape from the question.

questions.q: What does the archive experience suggest about visibility and mutual trust?
choices: Every personal story should be recorded and made public.
Disagreements are best excluded from community archives.
Friends have a right to know everything about one another.
Sharing frequent details does not necessarily create an honest relationship.
questions.explanation: Mara questions why she expects friends' details while editing her own life.

questions.q: Why does the retired nurse regard old arguments as evidence of caring?
choices: The street had no lasting conflicts.
Neighbours remained involved enough to disagree rather than withdraw.
People used to argue only about public transport.
The arguments were recorded by professional historians.
questions.explanation: The nurse describes disagreement as a sign of continued involvement.

questions.q: What is significant about the elderly man's refusal of sympathy?
choices: He thinks the archive should omit the shop altogether.
He wants the recording to be used as an advertisement.
He primarily wants the shop's meaning to be acknowledged, not his grief solved.
He has forgotten why he stopped visiting the street.
questions.explanation: The interview leads Mara to value attention over immediate advice.

questions.q: Why does Mara respect the contributor who rejects an audio recording?
choices: The archive should allow people to control how their experiences are shared.
A written description is always more historically accurate.
The contributor's story is less interesting than the nurse's.
The archive has run out of recording equipment.
questions.explanation: The paragraph treats refusal and a limited written record as legitimate choices.

questions.q: What problem does Mara see in turning the listening evening into a test of friendship?
choices: The event would have no audience without Jules.
Mara would have to pay for every visitor's ticket.
The recordings would become unsuitable for the archive.
Jules might feel obliged to prove commitment through attendance.
questions.explanation: She does not want an invitation to measure whether the friendship is still working.

questions.q: Why would one enjoyable weekend not be enough to repair the relationship?
choices: The archive is too far away for any visit.
It cannot automatically undo a year of superficial communication.
Jules would need to prepare a public speech.
Mara does not expect anyone to enjoy the event.
questions.explanation: Mara explicitly refuses to present one good evening as a complete repair.

questions.q: What is the function of allowing Jules to leave the event early?
choices: It makes the invitation genuinely flexible rather than demanding.
It ensures the group will finish the recordings early.
It allows Mara to avoid paying for admission.
It guarantees the event will not be crowded.
questions.explanation: The option respects Jules's comfort and choice.

questions.q: What would constitute meaningful progress in the relationship for Mara?
choices: Frequent photographs that make the friendship look active.
A formal plan for completing shared friendship goals.
Two people having an uncertain but honest conversation without performing closeness.
A promise that neither person will ever feel disappointed.
questions.explanation: The letter values authenticity and conversation over social performance.
